document.title: Fail fast when the macOS display is asleep or locked
document.summary: A new `scripts/check-macos-display.sh` exits non-zero with one line when the macOS display sleeps or the screen is locked, and the Vita3K, bench, and host `run` entry points call it before they build or open a window.
document.why: When the macOS display sleeps or the session locks, the host segfaults at window creation and Vita3K runs hang until a one-hour timeout, and unattended agent threads lose hours to that [according to the request](source:s1).

sources.label: T3 Code session · Oct 26
sources.gist: Máté asks for a shared startup check in the macOS GUI scripts that exits with one clear line when the display is asleep or the screen is locked, and does nothing on other platforms.

sources.label: PR #131
sources.title: fix(scripts): fail fast when the macOS display is asleep or locked
sources.gist: Adds the check and proves it with PATH stubs fed captured ioreg output.

lookFor: The request suggested `pmset -g powerstate IODisplayWranglerDevice` or `ioreg` for display power [(request)](source:s1). The display check calls `CGDisplayIsAsleep(CGMainDisplayID())` through `osascript -l JavaScript` instead. On macOS 26.7.1 that `pmset` query prints "Internal failure", Apple Silicon has no `IODisplayWrangler`, and GLFW makes the same `CGDisplayIsAsleep` call [(PR)](source:s2).
The host CMake `run` target also calls the check; the request asked for `vita3k.sh` and `bench.sh` "at least" [(request)](source:s1).

groups.title: The shared display check
groups.why: The request asks for the check in one shared place, as a few lines of shell with no new dependencies [(request)](source:s1).
groups.summary: `check-macos-display.sh` exits 0 off Darwin; on macOS it fails when `CGDisplayIsAsleep` reports the main display asleep or `ioreg -n Root -d1` shows a lock key.
lookFor: Subtle: when `osascript` fails or prints nothing, `asleep` is empty and the check passes, so a broken probe never blocks a run that might work.
The lock pattern `CGSSessionScreenIsLocked"=Yes` has no leading quote, so it matches both `"CGSSessionScreenIsLocked"` and `"kCGSSessionScreenIsLocked"` in any `IOConsoleUsers` entry.

groups.title: Entry points call the check
groups.why: The scripts that open a macOS window must run the check at startup [(request)](source:s1).
groups.summary: `vita3k.sh run|launch`, `bench.sh` for every target except `vita`, and the host CMake `run` target call the check before they build or open a window.
lookFor: `bench.sh vita3k` runs the check twice: once itself, which prints to the terminal, and again inside `vita3k.sh launch`, which prints into `log.txt`.
`bench.sh host` checks only before the build, so a display that sleeps during a long build still reaches the GLFW crash.

commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: fix(scripts): fail fast when the macOS display is asleep or locked
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
GLFW finds no monitor while the display sleeps and Vita3K stalls on a locked screen, so GUI entry points now check first and exit with one clear line.
